blocks.html: In a thread on August 3, as the Jason Arday scandal was just beginning to blow up, Tyler Austin Harper lamented that elite institutions select mediocre black candidates for symbolically important "first-ever" positions while passing over stronger black scholars. "There are plenty of talented black academics, and these elite schools step over their bodies to elevate scrubs who either come from rich families ([Claudine] Gay) or who let them feel the warm glow of the white man’s burden (Arday)."
While popular attention continued to struggle with the (easy) question whether Arday was an academic fraud and serial fabulist, Harper

essay published August 10, Tyler Austin Harper describes his experience with faculty hiring committees at Bates College and reflects that racial preferences operated much more aggressively than the sort of affirmative action he had expected and previously defended.
